title: Your Takeaway Order Probably Has More Salt Than It Says
hook: Almost half of takeaway meals tested had more salt than advertised — some serving nearly double the daily limit in one meal. Fish and chips, surprisingly, ranked among the lowest-salt options.
key_points: Almost half of the takeaway meals tested contained more salt than their advertised amount.
Some dishes delivered nearly twice the recommended daily salt limit in a single serving.
Pasta, pizza, and curries were often the saltiest options tested.
Classic fish and chips ranked among the lowest-salt choices — a surprising exception.
content_html: Advertised nutrition numbers on takeaway menus aren't always the whole story. A new study found that almost half of the takeaway meals tested contained more salt than advertised — and some dishes packed in nearly twice the recommended daily limit in a single serving.
extra_html: The pattern of which dishes were worst may surprise you: ScienceDaily reports that pasta, pizza, and curries were often the saltiest options, while classic fish and chips — not exactly known as a "light" choice — actually ranked among the lowest-salt meals tested. It's a reminder that a dish's reputation isn't a reliable guide to its sodium content, and that if you're watching your salt intake, the safer bet is checking posted nutrition information where it's available, rather than guessing by dish type.
